behavior: Adds cached postfix increment/decrement, copy plus/minus displacement, in-place subtract, subscript, and cross-const positional difference. Shared and mutable overloads are separated by full compiler const impl contexts. Payload T has no Clone or Default bound, verified through compiler generics and a non-Clone payload regression.

Postfix returns a Copy of all original cached state while mutating the receiver through existing navigation. Displaced copies leave the receiver unchanged, always consulting the supplied original owner even for offset zero. Subtraction rejects isize::MIN negation instead of invoking native signed undefined behavior.

Subscript implements native copy-plus-dereference using newly checked original-owner capture. It returns a safe reference tied to that explicit owner borrow; the mutable specialization obtains writable provenance from raw mutable storage capture. Null/end/dead-slot results are rejected before dereference. The stored original-owner pointer is compared but never dereferenced.

Native UBSan traces establish 19 output rows: two const-specialization labels plus17 observable behavior rows. After move, postfix old/current slots still denote destination payloads; after source refill, copied offset0 and subscript0 reload source101 while the original cursor still denotes destination1. Copy plus/minus, negative in-place subtraction, cross-const difference, cross-owner difference, end postfix transitions and mutable subscript writes match Rust.

Six new tests cover the native trace, non-Clone payload reference access, negation/addition/difference overflow, failed boundary reload preserving pointer state, wrong-owner errors, absent/dead slots, and empty-end dereference-free navigation. Full DynamicArray normal suite and all52 original native/Rust runtime names join; strict Miri includes original52, both cached suites, iterator/method tails and assignment behavior.

The eight exact inventory IDs include two separate template/child rows for positional subtraction and bind13 unique Rust public method bodies. They are scoped partial declaration bindings; this does not claim eight newly completed semantic APIs or new legacy declarations.
limitations: Assignment, mutable-to-const assignment, cached ordering comparisons and legacy Iterator Init/Initialize remain separate callable gaps. Existing detached convenience APIs are unchanged. Native free left-addition delegates to the same copy-plus behavior and is exercised, but no new exact declaration binding is claimed for its friend wrapper.

Navigation and copy arithmetic require the original owner reference even in native phases that only use cached pointer/index state. Navigation after original-owner destruction is not expressible through these checked methods. Original owner identity must match its captured address.

Safe subscript returns references governed by Rust borrowing/provenance. It is not a promise that arbitrary other saved raw cursors remain dereferenceable after conflicting reference access. Existing unsafe cached value/change_value retain their allocation lifetime and exclusivity obligations.

Wrong-owner, absent initialized-slot/block-end, null subscript and signed-overflow failures are checked Rust extensions outside the native defined dereference/arithmetic domain. No native UB execution is used as an oracle. Native ptrdiff_t cast behavior is evidenced on the pinned x86_64 platform only; cross-platform ABI/layout is not claimed.

Zero-sized payloads, retained zero-stride element mutation, incompatible block-end layout, corrupted/dead raw storage and unusual explicit enable_if template overrides remain outside capture domains. Native allocation/copy constructor failure resource lifetime differences remain actionable in their separate work.
